messages.subject: Wallace MEE print version Online Early!
messages.subject_clean: Wallace MEE print version Online Early!
messages.body_plain:
Just wanted to let everyone know that the final print version of the Wallace paper in Methods in Ecology and Evolution is now out Online Early! We're very excited to finally have the final version up online. Please let us know what you think.

http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/2041-210X.12945/full

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of New York

messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
messages.body_plain:
Dimitris,

Thanks for the suggestions. I was wondering why you selected those two algorithms in particular. If you have expertise with these algorithms and their implementation, and especially if you have R functions that work with them, we'd be interested in helping you develop some new modules for Wallace.

As for the independent evaluation, this would be a great addition, and I will add it to the list. Not everyone wants to evaluate by cross-validation, and we want to enable more flexibility for evaluating models.

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of New York

messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jamie and Wallace community,

These two algorithms are quite robust in over-fitting and require much less data (especially background data for the pseudo-absence). I use them for image classification (remote sensing) and have superior performance in terms of accuracy in comparison to others.

On the R side, am dummy :). I use some code - mostly ready-to-use by colleagues, adapted for my data). Thus, i cannot help on the development but on the use side.

The independent evaluation is very important. especially in invasion ecology (as am working on that) but also in cases that you model a species and use the results for targeted field campaigns for data collection and use of model output for conservation decisions.

I have real world data, so, if you need any help on testing modules on real data (rather on virtual species which i hate) let me know.

D.

messages.body_plain:
Dimitris,

Glad you're enjoying Wallace! Thanks a lot for the message about your error.

That's strange. Looks like there were problems mapping the raster with leaflet due to projection issues. Haven't seen an error like this recently.

What would be most helpful is if you could could tell me what your workflow was. I'd like to try and reproduce it to find the source of the error. Please also tell me if you input your own occurrence points or rasters.

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of NY

messages.subject: Re: ERROR: [on_request_read] connection reset by peer
messages.body_plain:
Dimitris,

Found the issue -- projection was NA for the rasters, as they were saved as .asc (ASCII), which does not retain projection information. When I defined their projection, saved them as .tif, and reloaded them, they worked fine. I implemented a quick fix that warns the user if the projection is NA, and then does not allow them to use mapping functions in component "Visualize Model Results". I've also added some new text to guidance text for the "User-specified Environmental Data" module that shows you how to define the projection and save the results in R. Finally, I made a Github issue here <https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/issues/116> and will close it once the master branch is pushed to CRAN.

For now, you can download the package from Github to see the new functionality. Please see directions here <https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace>.

Thanks a lot for the report! You've helped to make Wallace better =D

messages.subject: Re: input file format? single or multispecies?
messages.subject_clean: input file format? single or multispecies?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this information is in the guidance text for User-Specified Occurrences, and can also be found if you try to upload a csv without the right field names as an error in the log window.

Currently, Wallace only allows one species at a time, but we're working on a version that can allow for multiple single-species models during one session. I hope to release it in a couple of months or so. If you really want to try it before it's ready for showtime, please let me know.

J
